🔴 blocker  Vietnamese is the language of comments, lint messages and tool output in 82 of 87 files, and nothing guards against it
- key: tooling#language-of-code
- Where: eslint.config.js:22 (13 more messages at 26, 31, 36, 90, 96, 119, 124, 129, 137, 142, 153, 158, 164); eslint-rules/no-style-literals.js:85-87; eslint-rules/stryker-disable-reason.js:11; scripts/verify.mjs:15,32,39; scripts/canary.mjs:185,198,199,216; scripts/check-trace.mjs:91,94; scripts/serve-web.mjs:53; scripts/check-web-release.mjs:42; comments in nearly every file, for example src/core/api/client.ts:6, src/shell/Shell.tsx:75-80, jest.config.js:1-3
- Why: Counts over the 87 in-scope files (python3; the dispatcher's character class plus the letters a-grave, a-acute, a-tilde, e-grave, e-acute, i-grave, i-acute, o-grave, o-acute, o-tilde, u-grave, u-acute, y-acute, i-tilde, u-tilde): 552 Vietnamese lines in 82 files. By class: 52 dictionary lines in src/shell/strings/vi.ts (legitimate); 2 legitimate data lines (src/core/i18n/locale.ts:10 NATIVE_NAMES, the bilingual noscript at public/index.html:112); 29 developer-facing output lines (14 ESLint config messages, 4 custom-rule messages, 11 lines of script output, including the reports/verify.md header 'Gate | Result | Seconds' and the results 'green'/'RED'); about 469 comment lines. When a gate goes red, its message is the developer's only guidance. These messages are in Vietnamese and point to Vietnamese spec sections, so the agency team cannot use them. Every new file copies the comment style (82 of 87 already do). Any guard needs a wider net than the dispatcher's character class: that class has no plain Latin-1 accents, so it misses words such as 'dung', 'mau' and 'va' (written with those accents in the original) on 28 lines in 21 files across apps/metis (for example eslint-rules/no-style-literals.js:87, scripts/check-trace.mjs:4, plugins/with-ios-scene-lifecycle.js:4).
- Fix: Convention: English for code, comments, test titles, lint messages and tool output. Vietnamese appears only in src/**/strings/vi.ts, and vi-locale test data should import it from there instead of restating it. Rewrite the 29 output lines first, because they are the gates' user interface, then the comments file by file. Add a guard: scripts/check-language.mjs as `gate:language`, rejecting any non-ASCII letter outside an allowlist (src/**/strings/vi.ts, locale.ts:10, index.html:112). verify.mjs:9 already runs every `gate:*` script, so the package.json entry is the only wiring needed. Add a canary for the new gate in scripts/canary.mjs. When the ESLint messages become English, keep the token the canary matches: canary.mjs:135 expects 'spec 5.5' inside the message at eslint.config.js:90.
- approach-changing: no, a rewrite plus one small gate
- trigger: an agency developer imports src/design-system from src/core. `pnpm gate:lint` answers 'src/core is pure TypeScript (spec 3.2).' (eslint.config.js:119), a Vietnamese sentence citing a Vietnamese spec, and `pnpm verify` writes 'RED' into reports/verify.md
- guard-bypass: ESLint, Prettier, knip and tsc do not check what language a comment or message is in, and the canaries lock the current wording in place (canary.mjs:135 matches a substring of the Vietnamese message)
- design: yes, a language gate with an allowlist that scans for non-ASCII letters, not the dispatcher's diacritic class

🔴 blocker  Fixture ids, the API host and the storage key are retyped in config, mocks, scripts and tests instead of imported from one module
- key: src/mocks#fixture-ids-restated
- Where: src/platform/config.ts:4,8; src/mocks/handlers.ts:11-22; src/mocks/fixtures/shell.ts:32,34,43,51; scripts/check-web-release.mjs:14-17; src/platform/storage.web.ts:6 with public/index.html:13
- Why: The fixture modules export only whole objects, so every consumer types the ids again. Measured with rtk proxy grep -rnF over src, e2e, scripts and public: 'creative-studio' on 5 non-test lines in 3 files (config.ts:8, handlers.ts:12,14, fixtures/shell.ts:34,43) and on 152 test lines in 53 files; 'meridian-cgi-campaign' on 3 non-test lines and 94 test lines in 47 files; 'https://api.metis.test' in config.ts:4, again in handlers.ts:11, and on 13 test lines in 12 files; 'metis.locale' in storage.web.ts:6 and index.html:13. The release check keeps its own copy of four fixture strings ('Northwind Furniture Co.', 'Creative Production', 'Denny K.', 'Acme Holdings'). The production config is mock data: HOME (config.ts:8) puts fixture ids into the release bundle, so the root route of a release build redirects to /w/creative-studio/projects/meridian-cgi-campaign/overview (src/app/index.tsx:8) whatever the back end, and check-web-release.mjs does not look for ids. This is the production side of the owner's first complaint, and each new screen's fixture will be retyped the same way.
- Fix: handlers.ts:11 `const BASE = `${apiConfig.baseUrl}/workspaces/:workspaceId`` (import apiConfig from ../platform/config). At handlers.ts:12-22, derive from the fixtures: `new Map([creativeStudio, digitalProducts].map((s) => [s.workspace.id, s]))`, `const WORKSPACE = creativeStudio.workspace.id`, FORBIDDEN read from the tree. Export one `fixtureIds` object from src/mocks/fixtures (workspace, projects, forbidden project, display names) for tests, e2e and scripts, and build the check-web-release.mjs markers from it instead of a copy. In production, read the API host from the environment (EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL) and the home workspace from the API, not from fixture ids.
- approach-changing: no, one export and a handful of imports
- trigger: someone points apiConfig.baseUrl (config.ts:4) at a real host. handlers.ts:11 still matches only https://api.metis.test, and onUnhandledRequest is 'bypass' (mocks.web.ts:13, and mocks.ts:16 on native), so every request `pnpm web` and the e2e build used to mock now goes to the real network without a warning. Or someone renames 'Acme Holdings' in fixtures/shell.ts:32, and check-web-release.mjs:17 stops detecting that fixture in a release bundle
- guard-bypass: TypeScript cannot see that two strings in different files must be equal, and the 152 and 94 retyped test lines keep passing as long as every copy is edited together
- design: yes, a fixture-id module that src, e2e and scripts import

🟡 major  Pages outside a workspace (/me/*, /search) reload the shell with the HOME workspace, so the user loses the workspace they were in
- key: src/shell/Shell.tsx#home-fallback-loses-workspace
- Where: src/shell/Shell.tsx:82-85; src/platform/config.ts:6-8; src/shell/model.ts:70-73; src/shell/TopBar.tsx:97; ruling D-B23 at plan/2026-10-06-frontend-overview-screen.md:312, which lists its cost as "Cost: none"
- Why: The shell reads the workspace only from the URL and falls back to HOME.workspaceId when the URL has none. The My focus and Approvals links carry no workspace (model.ts:71-72), so following them from any workspace other than HOME loads Creative Studio's shell. The switcher, project tree, breadcrumb and the '+ New' target (TopBar.tsx:97) all change to a workspace the user did not pick, and the sidebar links then lead into Creative Studio. Four routes work this way today (myFocus, approvals, notifications, search), and plan C builds them.
- Fix: remember the last workspace seen on a /w/ route (a small context next to LocaleProvider, persisted like the locale) and fall back to HOME only on a cold start. In production, replace HOME with the user's default workspace from the API.
- approach-changing: yes, it reverses ruling D-B23
- trigger: on /w/digital-products/dashboard, press "My focus". /me/focus has no workspaceId, so useShell('creative-studio') runs and the sidebar shows Creative Studio and its project tree instead of Digital Products
- guard-bypass: Shell.test.native.tsx:114-115 opens /me/focus directly and asserts the HOME shell, which locks the fallback in as intended behaviour. e2e/web/routes.spec.ts:58-63 stops at the Digital Products dashboard URL, and no test navigates from a non-HOME workspace to a page outside a workspace
- design: yes, a remembered current workspace

🟡 major  A failed shell load cannot be retried, and the error text tells app users to reload a page
- key: src/shell/useShell.ts#no-retry
- Where: src/shell/useShell.ts:15-23; src/shell/Shell.tsx:112; src/shell/Sidebar.tsx:268-273; src/shell/Rail.tsx:47,61; src/shell/strings/en.ts:10; src/shell/strings/vi.ts:12
- Why: useShell fetches once per workspaceId (the effect's only dependency, useShell.ts:23). After a failure, or after the 10 s timeout (config.ts:4), the sidebar shows only "Could not load the menu. Reload the page to try again.", the rail shows only the menu button (Rail.tsx:61), and the breadcrumb is empty (Shell.tsx:23). The iOS and Android apps have no page to reload, so the only way out is to kill the app; on the web the user reloads the whole app. The overview screen already handles this (useOverview.ts:27 `retry: () => setAttempt((n) => n + 1)` and a Try again button), but the shell, which frames every screen, did not get the same treatment.
- Fix: give useShell the same attempt counter and return `{ result, retry }`. Render a secondary Button under the error in Sidebar (new prop `onRetry`). Reword `sidebar.menuError` in en.ts:10 and vi.ts:12 without "reload the page", and add a `sidebar.retry` key.
- approach-changing: no, it copies the overview's pattern
- trigger: the app starts on a phone with a flaky connection and getShell fails once; the drawer shows the reload sentence for the rest of the session
- guard-bypass: the device runs use the in-app mock layer (src/platform/mocks.ts:15-17), which answers at once, so the failure path never ran on a phone; and with no retry code, the unit tests have no recovery to check

🟡 major  A drill value with a comma passes the contract but comes back as two values after the link round trip
- key: src/core/api/overview.ts#drill-comma
- Where: src/core/api/overview.ts:27; src/core/routes.ts:79-83; src/shell/NotBuilt.tsx:22,44-47; node_modules/expo-router/build/link/href.js:83
- Why: The contract accepts any non-empty string as a drill value (`z.record(text, z.array(text).min(1))`). expo-router writes an array query parameter as `encodeURIComponent(value.toString())` (href.js:83), which turns ['high','critical'] into high%2Ccritical, and valuesOf (routes.ts:83) splits every value on ',' to get the array back. A single value that contains a comma therefore comes back as two values. The not-built page already lists the wrong filters (spec 4.3 rule 1), and plan C's WBS screen, which will read the same parameters, would filter on values that do not exist.
- Fix: forbid commas in the contract, at overview.ts:27: `const drill = z.record(text, z.array(text.regex(/^[^,]+$/, 'drill values cannot contain a comma')).min(1))`, and state the rule in the contract handed to the back end. Alternatively, encode each value before the router joins them.
- approach-changing: no, one schema line
- trigger: the server sends `drill: { category: ['Design, build'] }`; the link carries category=Design%2C%20build; filtersOf returns ['Design', ' build']
- guard-bypass: zod's `text` accepts commas, and every drill value in the fixtures is a comma-free id ('deliverable', '1.0', 'denny-k' in meridian.ts and showroom.ts), so no test hits the case

🟡 major  The trace gate counts skipped and todo tests as proof that a requirement is tested
- key: scripts/check-trace.mjs#skip-todo-count
- Where: scripts/check-trace.mjs:1-3, 12-21, 42-48
- Why: rootName follows any property access, so test.skip(...), it.skip(...), test.todo(...) and describe.skip(...) all resolve to a name in CALLS and their titles are collected (the header comment says .skip counts on purpose). A requirement whose only test is skipped or a todo therefore passes spec 9.1 rule 5 with no test run. Measured: 0 skip, todo or only calls in src and e2e today, so nothing exploits the gap yet.
- Fix: in titlesOf, ignore a call whose callee chain contains `skip` or `todo`, for example `const disabled = (n) => ts.isPropertyAccessExpression(n) ? ['skip', 'todo'].includes(n.name.text) || disabled(n.expression) : ts.isCallExpression(n) && disabled(n.expression)` checked on node.expression, and add both cases to check-trace.test.mjs.
- approach-changing: no, a filter in one function
- trigger: a developer adds BR-50 to a contract.yaml and writes `test.todo('BR-50: drill opens the filtered WBS')`; gate:trace prints that every code has a test and exits 0
- guard-bypass: Jest exits 0 on todo and skipped tests, and eslint.config.js loads no Jest plugin (there is no jest/no-disabled-tests), so nothing else rejects them

🟡 major  The lint rule that keeps UI text out of component code covers only src/design-system; the shell, screens and routes have none
- key: eslint.config.js#ui-text-rule-scope
- Where: eslint.config.js:78-100; src/shell/Rail.tsx:24; src/shell/NotBuilt.tsx:46; contrast src/shell/TopBar.tsx:113-117
- Why: The JSXText and literal selectors run on `src/design-system/**/*.tsx` only (eslint.config.js:81), so a shell, screen or route file can write `<Text>No items</Text>` or `aria-label="Close"` and gate:lint stays green while the vi locale shows English. In my scope the dictionary discipline holds (0 string-literal label, aria-label, placeholder or title props in the non-test tsx of src/shell, src/screens and src/app), but code builds two user-facing strings itself. The rail link's accessible name `${item.label} ${item.badge.count}` (Rail.tsx:24) hard-codes the word order, where TopBar.tsx:113-117 builds the same kind of name from a dictionary template. NotBuilt.tsx:46 builds the filter line `${name}: ${values.join(', ')}` the same way.
- Fix: widen the block's `files` to `src/{design-system,shell,screens,app}/**/*.tsx` (keep the test ignore) and add a selector for string and template literals in the `aria-label`, `label`, `placeholder` and `title` attributes. Move the two strings into the dictionaries (`sidebar.railLink: '{label} {count}'`, `page.filter: '{name}: {values}'`) and fill them with interpolate.
- approach-changing: no, configuration plus two dictionary keys
- trigger: a plan C screen writes `<Text>No items</Text>` under src/screens; gate:lint passes and the Vietnamese page shows 'No items'
- guard-bypass: the selectors are scoped to src/design-system, and the dictionary audit (src/core/i18n/audit.ts) compares en and vi keys without ever reading component code

🟡 major  Comments cite plan ruling ids and spec section numbers instead of giving the reason
- key: src#ruling-id-comments
- Where: 131 lines in 71 of the 87 in-scope files (dispatcher regex `R-[A-Z][0-9]+|FE-[0-9]+|D-B[0-9]+|spec [0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?`), for example src/shell/Shell.tsx:76-77 '(D-B22)', '(D-B23)'; src/core/api/client.ts:6 '(spec 3.3, 4.5, R-B15)'; src/app/index.tsx:6 '(R-B19, ...)'; the lint message at eslint.config.js:22 '(spec 7, R-B14)'. Also 9 dated history lines: src/platform/fonts.android.ts:5, src/shell/ProjectHeader.tsx:23, src/shell/Shell.tsx:99, src/shell/ProjectHeader.styles.ts:15, src/core/api/overview.ts:94, plugins/with-ios-scene-lifecycle.js:1,5, jest.config.js:47, playwright.config.ts:10
- Why: Each id points into a 919 KB Vietnamese plan that the agency will not read, and the code cannot show when a ruling is wrong. Shell.tsx:77 justifies the HOME fallback with '(D-B23)', whose plan entry (line 312) says it costs nothing, yet finding home-fallback-loses-workspace shows the cost. Dated lines such as fonts.android.ts:5 ('measured on 09/10/2026 on the emulator, strokes 36% thinner') are history: they belong in a commit message and go stale.
- Fix: replace each citation with the reason in one English line. For Shell.tsx:76-77, for example: "Pages outside a workspace (/me/..., /search) have no workspace in the URL, so the shell shows HOME's." Keep requirement ids only where a tool reads them (contract.yaml, and test titles for gate:trace), and move the dated detail to commit messages. The language gate can also reject `\b(R|D)-B[0-9]+\b|\bR-N[0-9]+\b|\bFE-[0-9]+\b` in comments outside contracts and test titles.
- approach-changing: no, a comment rewrite
- trigger: a developer has to change the shell fallback, and the comment's only reason is '(D-B23)'
- guard-bypass: no tool reads comment content; the trace gate needs ids in test titles, not in source comments
- design: yes, the id pattern added to the language gate

💭 nit  A start-up failure leaves a blank app, and the start-up logic sits in the one folder excluded from coverage and mutation
- key: src/app/_layout.tsx#startup-no-catch
- Where: src/app/_layout.tsx:11-19; src/platform/mocks.ts:21-25; jest.config.js:74-75; stryker.config.json:17
- Why: `mocks.then(() => setMocksReady(true))` has no rejection handler, so if startMocks() rejects, RootLayout returns null forever: a blank screen plus an unhandled rejection instead of the error. This already happened here: require('msw') threw "Property 'MessageEvent' doesn't exist" on the Android emulator (mocks.ts:21-25). On the web, a failed worker registration also rejects (node_modules/msw/lib/browser/index.mjs:1788), but an insecure context does not: MSW 2.15 falls back to FallbackHttpSource (index.mjs:3636-3645). This affects mock builds only, because release builds resolve at once. src/app is excluded from coverage and mutation on the claim that route files only join the shell and a screen (jest.config.js:74), but _layout.tsx holds the font and mock gating.
- Fix: `mocks.then(() => setMocksReady(true), (error) => { console.error(error); setMocksReady(true) })`, or move the gating into a tested hook in src/platform (for example useStartup) so the exclusion stays true.
- approach-changing: no

💭 nit  Route params are typed as plain strings although repeated query keys arrive as arrays
- key: src/shell/Shell.tsx#param-types
- Where: src/shell/Shell.tsx:82-85; src/app/w/[workspaceId]/projects/[projectId]/overview.tsx:7-11; contrast src/core/routes.ts:76-83
- Why: The generic arguments of useGlobalSearchParams and useLocalSearchParams declare workspaceId, projectId and scope as string, while the repo's own Params type and comment (routes.ts:76-82) say that a repeated key gives string[] [Source: src/core/routes.ts:79-82, the project's reading of expo-router; not re-checked in vendor code]. /me/focus?workspaceId=a&workspaceId=b would pass an array to useShell; isRouteId accepts it (an array is not '') and getShell requests /workspaces/a%2Cb/shell. The result is a 404 and the menu error, so the impact is low, but the types hide the case from every future route that reads params.
- Fix: read params as `Params` and narrow them with one shared helper in src/core/routes.ts (`const one = (v: string | string[] | undefined) => (typeof v === 'string' ? v : undefined)`), used by the shell and every route file.
- approach-changing: no

💭 nit  The invalidData scenario edits an untyped copy, so renaming the metric would silently stop it producing invalid data
- key: src/mocks/handlers.ts#untyped-clone
- Where: src/mocks/handlers.ts:43,49,61-62
- Why: `const copy = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(body))` at line 61 has type any, so `delete copy.metrics.blocked` is never type-checked. If the metric is renamed in overview.ts:63, the delete removes nothing and ?mock=invalidData serves valid data. The same clone is written three times (lines 43, 49, 61).
- Fix: `const metrics: Partial<Overview['metrics']> = { ...body.metrics }; delete metrics.blocked; return HttpResponse.json({ ...body, metrics })` (type-checked, so a rename fails to compile), plus one `clone = (body: Overview): Overview => JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(body))` helper for lines 43 and 49.
- approach-changing: no

💭 nit  index.html has a dead meta tag and a third copy of the locale key and list
- key: public/index.html#lang-script
- Where: public/index.html:5,13; src/platform/storage.web.ts:6; src/core/i18n/locale.ts:1-2
- Why: Line 5 uses the JSX spelling `httpEquiv`, but the HTML attribute is `http-equiv`, so the tag has no effect (and IE=edge is obsolete). Line 13 repeats the storage key 'metis.locale' and handles only 'vi', so the instruction in locale.ts:1-2 (adding a language takes one line there plus one strings file) misses a third place: a new locale would get the wrong lang attribute until the user first changes language.
